there are differences between school counseling and mental health counseling graduates in two of the eight core competencies as measured by the CPCE.
school counseling students and clinical mental health counseling students differ on the CPCE in two areas (i.e., helping relationships and group work).
the CPCE total score and two of the subscale scores (Helping Relationships, Group Work) are statistically different based on program specialty.

how the CACREP competencies for school counselors are different from the CACREP clinical mental health counseling competencies.
the emerging leadership of school counselor trainees as it relates to the provision of mental health counseling services.
the preparation of school counselors and the need for more mental health counseling training.

school counseling graduates do not have the same competencies for mental health counseling as clinical mental health counselor trainees.
the school counselor trainees in this sample did not score significantly different than clinical mental health counselor trainees on the CPCE.

school counselors and mental health counselors have different competencies and training needs.

there are differences in the counseling competencies of students who are training in school counseling versus students training in clinical mental health, and the differences are in the areas of group counseling and helping relationships.

school counseling students need more training and experience in the areas of helping relationships and group work in order to be effective in providing mental health counseling services in the schools.
